expectations.text: Advocates against the winter extension and prioritizes repairing the inaccessible side ramp using the same budget.
expectations.evidence: "I don't think we should extend library hours this winter while the side ramp remains inaccessible" establishes opposition; "the same budget could repair the side ramp" and "I'd put this winter's money into the ramp" establish the alternative priority.

expectations.text: Retains 14 visits per night in last January's count, single staffed entrance, and no added security funding without changing implications into proven harm.
expectations.evidence: "Last January's count recorded 14 evening visits per night"; "the current proposal would staff only one entrance and add no security funding" retain the evidence. "We ought to fund the support those hours require" is an argued priority, not a claim of an observed security incident.

expectations.text: Acknowledges potential benefit to shift workers without inventing their preferences or surveys.
expectations.evidence: "Later hours could help shift workers who struggle to get there during the day" acknowledges a plausible conditional benefit without inventing survey results or claiming that shift workers collectively favor the plan.

expectations.text: 120–180 words, one paragraph, no invented personal experience or consensus.
expectations.evidence: 141 whitespace-delimited words in one paragraph. "My priority" and "I'd put" identify the writer's stance; no personal incident or resident consensus is fabricated.

review_method: Independent single blind agent review; not human feedback
